prompts: We playtested two versions of the Pixel Arena tutorial and have to pick one for the next release. The export and its notes are in {WS}/telemetry. Should we ship B instead of A? Give a recommendation a skeptical lead would accept. Record it in {WS}/result.json with ship_b, sessions_a, sessions_b, completion_rate_a, completion_rate_b and p_value.
answers:
[goal] Pick A or B for the tutorial release, backed by the playtest export.
[action] Parsed `telemetry/playtest_ab.csv`, deduped by `session_id` (70 duplicated resends, all identical rows), normalized variant casing/whitespace, computed completion rates and a two-proportion z-test.
[result] 1,800 unique sessions (900 per variant); A: 342/900 = 38.0%; B: 420/900 = 46.7%; gain +8.7 pts; z = 3.72, p = 0.00020 (two-sided). Ship B, significant at 5%. Assumptions: dedupe keeps one row per session (all duplicate rows identical); two-proportion z-test as the 5% significance check; no other confounders (e.g., match_minutes) explored, but no reason to expect them to flip the result.
[next] Ship B per the release rule. Note: result.json records `ship_b: true`; the 5% rule is met either way, so the gain direction and p-value agree.
